title: Template-candidate resolution walks out of the theme root because the sanitiser runs on the encoded form and the sink decodes it
index_line: T-0016 · CODE_EXEC · slug sanitiser preserves %2e%2f while the resolver decodes and includes · php/all-CMS · corroborated
invariant_violated: A sanitiser and the sink that consumes its output are assumed to agree on the representation of the string. This sanitiser preserves percent-escaped octets (it rewrites literal dots and truncates at literal slashes), and the template resolver downstream decodes them — so a traversal that is impossible in the literal form is trivial in the encoded one.

mechanism.does: the page slug arrives from the request (query string or POST body; the body wins) and names a template candidate
the slug is sanitised — literal dots rewritten, literal slashes truncate the value, percent-escaped octets deliberately survive
the candidate is built by continuing a real theme directory that starts with `page-` (page-templates) and is then decoded and joined onto the theme root
the resolver walks `../` sequences that only exist after decoding, and lands on a readable local `.php` outside the active theme directories
the chosen file is included, so a readable `.php` anywhere on disk is now executed in the web-server context
with register_argc_argv on, a readable CLI script (pearcmd.php) is reached through the same include and turned into arbitrary file write with attacker content

source.http.request.value: the slug parameter — POST body is preferred over the query string, so a GET-only filter misses half the traffic

sink.file.read.value: the include/require of a path derived from a request-named template candidate

encoding.path.value: percent-escaped traversal (%2e%2e%2f, double-encoded %252e%252e%252f, mixed case hex) — the form that survives a sanitiser which only rewrites literals

guard.resolve-check.value: the theme-root prefix / realpath check — it is applied to the pre-decode string, which is why it passes

preconditions.expr: the active (child or parent) theme has a top-level directory whose name starts with `page-`; without it the candidate never begins inside the theme and the climb-out is impossible
the slug reaches template resolution after sanitisation (WordPress: get_page_template()); a valid object id is required or the 404 short-circuits before the vulnerable code
build is inside the affected range and the resolver is not shadowed by a plugin/theme filter

check.spec: grep -m1 "wp_version =" wp-includes/version.php  # affected: 4.7.0–7.1.1; fixed: 7.1.2 and backports to 4.7.37

preconditions.expr: register_argc_argv on promotes the include from information leak to file write (PEAR pearcmd.php readable on the host)

success: the response body is the content of a file that is not a template of the active theme (an OPML or RSS core file served from a normal page URL is the classic tell)
traversal arrives percent-encoded and the slug begins with a `page-` directory name before the climb-out — literal `../` never works
a request carrying pearcmd plus `+config-show` confirms argv reachability, and `+config-create` writes attacker PHP to disk
failure_like: the sanitiser rewrites `%2e`/`%2f` as well as `.`/`/` — then the encoded form dies too
the resolver re-normalises and re-checks containment after decoding
false_positive: a 200 carrying theme output for an existing page — no traversal happened; the tell is foreign file content, not a status code
blocked traversal that still returns the theme's 404 template
attributing file content to the include when the same path is separately web-reachable (a real file in the web root) — check the path is outside the docroot

hazards: the theme precondition is not decoration: without a `page-` top-level directory the payload has nothing to continue, and scanners that skip this check report noise
POST is preferred over GET for the slug in this implementation — a GET-only WAF rule is bypassed by moving the parameter to the body
PEAR's pearcmd.php exists on the official php Docker image and on default cPanel installs below PHP 8.5 — that is what turns LFI into write without an upload
non_transfers: frameworks whose template resolver refuses any path containing a separator before decoding
engines that build the candidate from a fixed whitelist of template names rather than from a request-named slug
runtimes without an in-process include of arbitrary readable files (a read-only file sink is FILE_READ, not this)
